summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Willow Payments through data handling and retention controls in the Console and API. Demo covered request storage toggles, automated PII redaction, custom redact rules, retention windows, and enterprise features (KMS, SSO, audit logs). Customer asked detailed questions about guarantees, deletion timelines, and POC setup. Agreed next steps: send security docs, provision trial tenant, schedule a security deep-dive, and run a short POC to validate retention and redaction on their payloads.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE. With me is Arjun our SE, and Nina from product. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Samir Nair: Good, thanks. Samir here, CTO at Willow. We've got Lara, Ethan and Priya on as well.
[00:13] Maya Chen: Awesome. Today we'll run through our data handling and retention controls — quick overview, then Arjun will jump into Console demo showing logging redaction, PII detection, and the request-storage toggles. We'll leave time for questions.
[00:25] Lara Gomez: Sounds good, high level — our security team is mainly focused on preventing any storage of payment card data or PII in logs, and we need audit trails for compliance.
[00:33] Arjun Patel: Totally. We'll show both automatic redaction and how you can define custom rules. Also how retention windows work and the toggle that disables request storage entirely for a tenant.
[00:42] [01:00] Arjun Patel: Ok jumping into the Console — you'll see on the left our settings page, under Data Handling there are a few toggles. First is "Request Storage" — default ON for hosted tenants, but you can flip it OFF which means no request bodies are persisted to disk; only minimal metadata for billing/metrics.
[01:20] Ethan Price: Quick question, when you flip it off, is there any ephemeral caching that still holds data?
[01:25] Arjun Patel: Great question. We still use KV cache in the serving runtime for active sessions (to optimize latency), but that's in-memory and not written to persistent storage. For strict off tenants we flush KV cache on session end and it's never persisted to disk; that's part of our Private/Dedicated guarantees too.
[01:45] [01:50] Lara Gomez: And what about ability to redact specific fields in payloads — like card numbers or SSNs?
[01:55] Arjun Patel: We have a layered approach: automated PII detectors (regex + ML models) that catch common things, plus custom redact rules you can add by JSON path or regex. You can choose to mask values, replace with token, or drop the field entirely.
[02:12] Maya Chen: To add — we publish default policy templates for payments companies that proactively mask PAN-like patterns.
[02:20] [02:40] Priya Rao: Are the ML detectors configurable per-tenant? We have some internal field names that are nonstandard.
[02:45] Arjun Patel: Yes, per-tenant config. You can upload custom rules, test them in a sandbox, and there's a simulator in the Console that shows what would be redacted.
[03:00] [03:10] Samir Nair: What's the SLA on deletion? If we need to ensure data is removed within X hours after a retention window change, how does that work?
[03:20] Arjun Patel: Retention windows are enforced by our lifecycle job. For hosted customers, once a retention policy expires, data is marked for deletion and purged typically within 24–72 hours depending on batch windows — we can agree an RTO in Dedicated contracts. For Private deployments you control the purge schedule.
[03:40] Lara Gomez: Do you provide proof of deletion?
[03:43] Nina Ortiz: We provide audit events for deletion actions, and we can share logs showing the purge jobs. For enterprise deals we include attestations in the security pack.
[03:55] [04:10] Ethan Price: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys? We need to keep control of encryption keys for certain datasets.
[04:17] Arjun Patel: Yes, CMK via integrations with major cloud KMS providers, and for on-prem/private we support HSM integrations. Keys are used to encrypt persistent storage; when request-storage is off, there's nothing to encrypt on disk but we still encrypt other artifacts.
[04:35] [04:50] Priya Rao: What about audit trail fidelity — we need per-request traceability without exposing PII.
[04:57] Maya Chen: You can keep metadata like request ID, timestamps, model, route, token counts — that data is separate from request payloads and can be retained for observability. We also support masked audit logs where sensitive values are replaced but the structure remains.
[05:15] [05:30] Arjun Patel: Demo time — I'll upload a sample payload with a mock PAN and email so you can see redaction live.
[05:35] [05:45] [06:00] Arjun Patel: Paste payload into simulator... hitting run... ok you can see the detector flagged PAN-like pattern and email, it replaced the PAN with <REDACTED_CARD> and masked email partially like j***@example.com.
[06:20] Lara Gomez: Hmm, email mask is good, but can we tokenize instead so we can map back to our internal identifier?
[06:28] Arjun Patel: Absolutely — we support tokenization where we return a reversible token to your KMS-wrapped store; reversal requires authorized key access. That tokenization can be configured to use your key material.
[06:40] [07:00] Ethan Price: Is tokenization compatible with streaming responses / generation? We have flows that stream back partial outputs.
[07:08] Arjun Patel: Yes, tokenization happens at ingress before the request hits the model. For streaming, the model only sees the tokenized value, and the response can be detokenized by your side if you have the key, or we can detokenize in a secure path if you authorize it.
[07:30] [07:45] Priya Rao: Any false positives we've seen? The ML detector sometimes flags invoice numbers that look like card numbers.
[07:50] Arjun Patel: We see that occasionally; that's why the per-tenant custom rule layer exists. You can create exceptions by path or pattern and test them in the simulator. We also log detector confidence so you can review low-confidence matches.
[08:10] [08:20] Samir Nair: How do these features differ across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[08:28] Arjun Patel: Hosted gives you the full Console and default controls. Dedicated gives SLA-backed throughput and the ability to set stricter data deletion SLOs and isolated storage. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you control of key material and complete control over persistence and job schedules — useful if you have regulatory constraints.
[08:50] Lara Gomez: For compliance we need SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs kept for 7 years — do you support long-term archival without payloads?
[08:58] Nina Ortiz: Yes, we support exporting masked audit logs to your S3 or cloud archive; those logs can be configured to exclude payloads but keep metadata and event traces. RBAC and SAML are standard enterprise integrations.
[09:20] [09:45] Arjun Patel: Back to Console, there's also a policy engine — you can create retention policies per route, per team, or per model. For example payments-route => retention 30 days; analytics-route => 90 days. We'll show creating one now.
[10:05] [10:20] Arjun Patel: Creating a policy: name, selector, retention window, actions (mask, drop, notify). I'll set payments-route -> 30 days and enable "auto-purge". Save. Now we can simulate older entries being purged.
[10:40] Priya Rao: If we change a retention window from 90 to 30, do you immediately purge data older than 30 days?
[10:50] Arjun Patel: The lifecycle job runs on a cadence — for hosted tenants it's batched. We'll include the timing details in the security docs; for Dedicated we can negotiate a tighter timeframe as part of SLAs.
[11:05] [11:20] Maya Chen: Quick product note — we recently added a "retention dry run" that flags data that would be purged without actually deleting it; useful for audits.
[11:30] [11:45] Lara Gomez: Can we get a report that shows what would be purged?
[11:48] Arjun Patel: Yes — dry-run outputs a CSV with request IDs, timestamps, route, and masked metadata.
[12:00] [12:15] Samir Nair: Regarding legal — e-discovery or lawful requests — do you have controls to put a hold?
[12:22] Nina Ortiz: We support legal hold per-selector; when active it prevents auto-purge for matching records and emits audit flags. We keep logs of holds and releases.
[12:40] [12:55] Ethan Price: For the POC, we'd like to push 100k requests with real-ish payloads (sanitized) to validate redaction and retention. How quickly can we get a tenant?
[13:05] Arjun Patel: We can spin up a trial tenant and give you toggles to enable/disable request storage, plus the redaction rules. Usually takes 1–3 business days to provision. For a larger POC we can provision Dedicated trial capacity.
[13:25] [13:40] Lara Gomez: Any third-party processors involved? Where does the data flow go?
[13:48] Arjun Patel: For hosted, data lives on Redwood-managed storage in region you choose. For Dedicated it's in isolated buckets per-customer. We don't share customer data with third parties; we use cloud providers for infra and we list subprocessors in our security package.
[14:05] [14:20] Priya Rao: Can we run a small benchmark to measure extra latency from redaction/tokenization?
[14:28] Arjun Patel: Yes — redaction runs at ingress and typically adds a few ms depending on complexity and detector load; tokenization may add slightly more if it calls external KMS. We can include latency breakdown in the POC.
[14:45] [15:00] Maya Chen: I'll summarize next steps at the end — but quick check, any outstanding blockers?
[15:07] Lara Gomez: Security docs, proof of deletion, and CMK support are blockers for us. If those are satisfactory we'll move forward with POC.
[15:15] Maya Chen: Great — we'll send the SOC2/ISO docs and the KMS guide after the call.
[15:20] [15:40] Arjun Patel: Final demo item — API level toggles: you can set per-route headers to disable storage for a given request, e.g., X-Redwood-Store: false. That way you get fine-grained control without tenant-wide change.
[15:55] Ethan Price: Nice, per-request toggle is important for mixed workloads.
[16:05] Priya Rao: About the simulator logs — can we export examples of redacted vs original for our auditors?
[16:12] Arjun Patel: We don't export originals once redacted in the simulator by default, but for audits we can provide sample sanitized sets and logs that show detector behavior without exposing raw sensitive values.
[16:30] [16:45] Samir Nair: Any notes on cost implication — does tokenization or KMS calls increase per-request cost?
[16:52] Maya Chen: Tokenization and KMS calls can add a small per-request charge depending on your contract; we'll include pricing options in the sheet. There's also cost tradeoffs between batching and retention (longer retention increases storage costs).
[17:10] [17:30] Maya Chen: Alright last bit — security deep-dive. Lara, would your team prefer next Tuesday or Thursday?
[17:38] Lara Gomez: Thursday looks better for us. I'll confirm times.
[17:45] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll send calendar invites.
[17:55] [18:10] Samir Nair: Thanks for the demo, this was helpful.
[18:15] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with docs and tenant.
[18:22] [18:30] END OF TRANSCRIPT.
